quiz.q: What did India's October CPI release show?
options: Inflation fell below 4%
Inflation rose to 6.09%, above the RBI's 6% upper band
Inflation was unchanged at 5.54%
Deflation for the first time
quiz.explain: MoSPI said retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October from 5.54%, breaching the RBI's tolerance band ahead of the Dec 4 policy meeting.

quiz.q: Which Polish law did President Nawrocki veto on Nov 13?
options: The 2027 budget
The second law implementing the EU Digital Services Act
The anti-alcohol law
The nuclear special act
quiz.explain: He vetoed the fast procedure for blocking illegal online content, calling it censorship, leaving the DSA only partly implemented.

quiz.q: Why did the US reportedly lose its measles-elimination status?
options: A single imported case
More than 12 months of continuous transmission
A CDC funding lapse
WHO changed its definitions
quiz.explain: PAHO revokes the status after a year of uninterrupted spread; the US had held it since 2000 and has over 5,400 cases this year.

lessonQuiz.q: Which statement about upper houses is correct?
options: The Polish Senate can permanently block any bill
The US Senate must pass every bill in the same text as the House
The Rajya Sabha can bring down the government
All three upper houses are directly elected
lessonQuiz.explain: The US chambers are equal partners. Poland's Senate can be overruled by the Sejm, and India's Rajya Sabha cannot remove the government, which answers to the Lok Sabha.

lessonQuiz.q: In Poland, most presidential acts need the prime minister's countersignature. What does that mean in cohabitation?
options: The president can do nothing alone
The president's main independent tools are constitutional prerogatives such as the veto and Tribunal referral
The prime minister can veto laws
Countersignature applies only to foreign policy
lessonQuiz.explain: Prerogatives listed in the Constitution, like the veto, need no countersignature, so a president from the rival camp relies on them.

lessonQuiz.q: Why does India's President rarely block legislation?
options: The President has no role in lawmaking
The President acts on ministerial advice and must assent if a bill is passed again
The Supreme Court signs bills instead
Bills go straight from the Lok Sabha into force
lessonQuiz.explain: India's President can return a non-money bill once, but must assent if Parliament passes it again; the role is largely formal.
